newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik leader faces second operation after attack.
newsitem.headline: Tajik leader faces second operation after attack.

text.p: Tajikistan authorities said on Thursday President Imomali Rakhmonov would have to undergo a second operation to remove all the shrapnel from a leg wound suffered in an assassination attempt on Wednesday.
An official in Rakhmonov's administration was unable to say when the new surgery on the president's right leg would take place.
"Surgeons operated for about an hour but they failed to remove all the shrapnel," said the official, speaking on condition of anonymity.
Two people were killed and 60 were injured in the attack, which occurred when Rakhmonov visited the northern town of Khudjand, according to the president's official spokesman Zafar Saidov.

Rakhmonov, 45, had a grenade thrown at his feet while getting out of a car. The president was hurt in the legs but was able to limp down the steps from his aircraft when he returned to the capital Dushanbe.
"The president's health is not endangered," Saidov said on Wednesday.
Tajikistan, a former Soviet republic, is still reeling from a four-year civil war in which tens of thousands of people were killed.
Armed groups still roam the mountain state, which borders Afghanistan and China.
A spokesman for Tajikistan's armed Islamic opposition, Rakhmonov's main foe in the civil war, told Reuters the group had no connection with the attack.
The Tajik official said the government would meet on Thursday and issue a declaration calling on the Commonwealth of Independent States, which unites 12 former Soviet republics, to fight terrorism.
